title: Volkswagen ID. Tiguan tanıtıldı: ID.4 modelinin yerini alıyor
summary: Volkswagen, ID.4 ve ID.5 modellerinin yerini alacak yeni elektrikli SUV modeli ID. Tiguan'ı duyurdu. Model, fiziksel tuşları ve 600 km menziliyle dikkat çekiyor.
body:
Volkswagen ID. Tiguan, markanın ID.4 ve ID.5 modellerinin yerini almak üzere resmi olarak tanıtıldı. Şirketin MEB+ platformu üzerine inşa edilen yeni elektrikli SUV, geleneksel SUV hatları ve 600 kilometreye varan sürüş menziliyle öne çıkıyor.

## Fiziksel düğmeler ve yenilenen iç mekân

Motor1 ve InsideEVs'in aktardığına göre Volkswagen, önceki elektrikli modellerinde eleştirilen dokunmatik kumandalar yerine ID. Tiguan modelinde fiziksel tuşlara geri döndü. Direksiyon üzerinde ve orta konsolda iklimlendirme ile ses ayarları için gerçek düğmeler yer alıyor. Kabinde 10 inçlik dijital gösterge paneli ve 15 inçlik bilgi-eğlence ekranının yanı sıra ilk kez 12 inçlik bir ön yolcu ekranı seçeneği sunuluyor. Sürücü göstergesinde istenirse Golf IV tarzı klasik bir gösterge teması da seçilebiliyor.

## Volkswagen ID. Tiguan teknik özellikleri ve menzili

Yeni ID. Tiguan üç farklı motor seçeneğiyle geliyor:

* 58 kWh bataryalı, 187 beygir güç üreten arkadan itişli giriş versiyonu.
* 77 kWh bataryalı, 281 beygir güç sunan arkadan itişli versiyon.
* 77 kWh bataryalı, 295 beygir güç sunan 4MOTION dört çeker versiyon.

77 kWh bataryalı arkadan itişli model WLTP standartlarına göre 600 kilometreye kadar menzil sunuyor. Araçta 32 litrelik ön bagaj (frunk), tek pedalla sürüş ve harici cihazları şarj etmeyi sağlayan V2L desteği bulunuyor. Avrupa'da ön siparişleri 13 Ekim'de 42 bin 695 avrodan başlayan fiyatlarla açılacak otomobilin teslimatları 2027 başında başlayacak; Türkiye satış tarihi ve fiyatı ise henüz açıklanmadı.

**Neden önemli?** Volkswagen, dokunmatik arayüzlerden uzaklaşarak geleneksel kullanım ergonomisini elektrikli altyapıyla buluşturuyor. Bu adım, markanın ID serisinde kullanıcı deneyimi açısından en çok eleştirilen noktaları düzeltme kararlılığını gösteriyor.

source_texts.title: VW’s ID Tiguan Replaces ID 4 With Up To 373 Miles Of Range
source_texts.summary: VW has announced rear- and all-wheel drive versions of the ID Tiguan with 58 kWh and 77 kWh battery packs
source_texts.text:
- The new ID Tiguan replaces both the VW ID 4 and ID 5.
- VW’s latest electric SUV uses its familiar MEB+ platform.
- The ID Tiguan will launch in North America, but timing is unconfirmed.
Like many of its competitors, Volkswagen has realized the best way to convince motorists to buy an EV is not to make it look weird or give it an odd name, but instead to create an EV that looks and sounds familiar. This is exactly what it’s done with the new ID Tiguan, built to replace the ID 4 and ID 5, and leaning into a more traditional SUV design that should better appeal to typical VW buyers.
Just like the Cupra Raval, VW ID Polo, and VW ID Cross, the new ID Tiguan uses the company’s latest MEB+ platform. This architecture supports three distinctive versions and two different battery packs. Sitting at the base of the range will be a rear-wheel-drive version using a 58-kWh battery. VW hasn’t provided chemistry details about this pack, nor has it said whether it’s the same usable 58-kWh pack that had been offered in North America’s ID 4. What we do know is this base model is rated at 187 horsepower.
Positioned in the middle of the range will be a more powerful, 282 hp rear-wheel drive model with a larger 77 kWh battery. Shoppers who want all-wheel drive traction will be able to order the ID Tiguan in a single 4MOTION all-wheel drive configuration, producing a combined 295 hp and also using the 77-kWh pack.
VW says the new ID Tiguan can travel up to 373 miles (600 km) on a single charge under the WLTP cycle. This is presumably for the rear-wheel-drive, 77-kWh model, although that has yet to be confirmed. Prospective buyers of the ID Tiguan will be pleased to know the 58-kWh version can haul up to 3,968 lbs (1,800 kg), while the 77 kWh models are good for 4,409 lbs (2,000 kg).
A Fresh New Design
The ID Tiguan’s design immediately distinguishes it from the ID 4 and ID 5. VW says it uses the company’s Pure Positive design language, boosting its presence and making it look more modern. Like the ID Polo and ID Cross, which it shares its platform with, the ID Tiguan also has several design similarities to those models.
The most obvious of these is the intricate LED daytime running lights and light bar stretching the width of the front fascia. Instead of a traditional grille, VW has added a pair of black intakes near the base of the bumper. There’s nothing radical about the EV’s side profile, but the shoulder line running from the corner of the headlight, along the doors, and across the tailgate catches the eye. At the rear are an intriguing set of taillights with bold LED graphics and four narrow illuminated stripes connecting them. Glowing emblems have also been added to the front and rear of the ID Tiguan.
A Cabin With Real Buttons
Arguably more important than how the EV looks from the outside is what the interior is like. By comparison, the old ID 4 and ID 5 feel very outdated. It starts with the new steering wheel that uses physical buttons for the cruise control and audio settings, rather than the silly piano black plastic haptic switches of old.
Additionally, the ID Tiguan has a larger digital instrument cluster built into the dashboard, rather than just perched on top of it like this model’s predecessors. This cluster even includes a very cool ‘Retro’ theme which displays four traditional gauges. A larger infotainment system has also been added, although VW hasn’t mentioned how big it is. A passenger display will also be available.
Then there are the buttons. VW was almost burned at the stake for its silly touch-sensitive controls used across its outgoing generation of cars. There are none in sight with the ID Tiguan. Located under the central air vents are nine physical switches to control the HVAC, including the temperature and fan speed, all with a lovely, knurled metal finish. There’s also a small volume knob on the center console and two wireless phone chargers.
The materials throughout also appear slightly nicer, particularly the soft-touch surfaces on the tunnel and door panels, although we’ll reserve final judgment until we actually see it in person. A full range of options has yet to be announced, but VW says the ID Tiguan will be available with optional massaging, heated, and ventilated front seats, a Harman Kardon audio system, and a panoramic sunroof. It also supports a Digital Key, so owners can use their smartphone to lock, unlock, and start the EV.
VW has confirmed the ID Tiguan will launch in North America, but it’s not yet ready to say when it will arrive locally. In the meantime, pre-sales across Europe will start on October 13 with prices kicking off at €42,695 ($47,900). Deliveries will start early next year.

source_texts.title: Volkswagen ID.4 Is Dead: Meet Its New Electric SUV Replacement
source_texts.summary: The new ID. Tiguan replaces the ID.4 with a more traditional SUV design and an interior packed with physical controls.
source_texts.text:
Volkswagen ID.4 Is Dead: Meet Its New Electric SUV Replacement
The new ID. Tiguan replaces the ID.4 with a more traditional SUV design and an interior packed with physical controls.
The Volkswagen ID.4, as we know it, is dead, and Volkswagen is officially announcing its replacement. Meet the new-and-improved ID. Tiguan.
The new ID. Tiguan will succeed the ID.4 and the European-market ID.5, bringing a more traditional SUV design, a redesigned interior, and up to 373 miles (600 kilometers) of WLTP range in Europe.
The electric SUV will launch in Germany and other European markets in early 2027, while the gasoline-, diesel-, and hybrid-powered Tiguan will continue alongside it.
2027 Volkswagen ID. Tiguan
Volkswagen is moving away from the softer crossover shape of the ID.4 and ID.5 with the ID. Tiguan. The new model gets a more upright, muscular look with sharper body lines and sculpted sheet metal. The company is even bringing back classic pull-style exterior door handles—praise be.
Inside, there’s even more to look at. Volkswagen says it has focused heavily on material quality and intuitive controls, addressing some of the complaints surrounding its earlier ID models, including those annoying touch-capacitive controls.
The ID. Tiguan gets physical controls for important functions, including the air conditioning, while the multifunction steering wheel also uses physical buttons instead of touch-sensitive controls. An illuminated controller in the center console handles audio volume and track or station selection.
The ID. Tiguan will launch with three different powertrain options in Europe, but it’s unclear if all three options will make it to the US:
- 58.0-kWh battery, 188 horsepower, rear-wheel drive
- 77.0-kWh battery, 281 horsepower, rear-wheel drive
- 77.0-kWh battery, 295 horsepower, all-wheel drive
Volkswagen says the ID. Tiguan will offer up to 373 miles (600 km) of WLTP range, depending on the configuration. VW has also improved its towing capacity, with the 58.0-kWh model able to tow up to 3,968 pounds (1,800 kg), while the 77.0-kWh versions can tow up to 4,409 pounds (2,000 kg).
There's also a 1.1-cubic-foot (32-liter) frunk, while the rear cargo area offers up to 18.9 cubic feet (534 liters) of storage.
The ID. Tiguan will also support vehicle-to-load functionality. A PowerSocket adapter connects to the charging port and allows the battery to power external devices like an electric grill or e-bike.
The dashboard is dominated by a 10.0-inch digital instrument cluster for the driver, a 15.0-inch central infotainment screen, and, for the first time on a European Volkswagen, an optional 12.0-inch display dedicated to the front passenger.
Volkswagen also offers a new "Retro" mode that can transform the driver's digital gauges into a recreation of the blue-and-red instrumentation from the Golf IV. The central screen can also display a virtual garage featuring six iconic Volkswagen models: the Golf I, Golf II Country, Golf IV, Tiguan I, Race Touareg, and Beetle.
One-pedal driving will come standard, while an available Connected Travel Assist system adds features like assisted lane changes on highways and traffic-light recognition. Volkswagen says the system can automatically bring the vehicle to a stop at red lights.
Other available features include massaging, ventilated, and electrically adjustable front seats, a panoramic sunroof, and a 480-watt Harman Kardon sound system.
The new ID. Tiguan will come in four trim levels in Europe: Trend, Life, Style, and R-Line. Pre-orders in Germany and several other European countries begin October 13, with prices starting at €42,695, or roughly $48,000 at current exchange rates.
The ID. Tiguan is scheduled to launch in early 2027.

source_texts.title: The Volkswagen ID. Tiguan Looks Like A Big Upgrade Over The ID.4
source_texts.summary: This new crossover has more buttons, one-pedal driving, and even a frunk.
source_texts.text:
The Volkswagen ID. Tiguan Looks Like A Big Upgrade Over The ID.4
This new crossover has more buttons, one-pedal driving, and even a frunk.
- Volkswagen on Friday unveiled the ID. Tiguan, its replacement for the ID.4.
- It serves up upgrades in key areas, including better software and a frunk, something the old ID.4 did not have.
- It goes on sale in Europe in early 2027, and will hit the U.S. sometime after that.
Goodbye, ID.4. Volkswagen is replacing its compact EV crossover with this, the ID. Tiguan. It’s about the same size as the old car, but with a more familiar name and some big changes that should make it a much better electric vehicle.
The ID.4 first went on sale in 2021. It was known for being a spacious EV and a good value, especially since at one point it was made in the U.S. and qualified for the EV tax credit. But over its run, people also complained about some key features, like the car’s software and some elements of the driving experience.
Gallery: Volkswagen ID. Tiguan (2027)
Earlier this year, VW announced that it was stopping production of the EV in the U.S. in favor of gas vehicles, leaving it without a mainstream electric offering in this market. Now the ID. Tiguan is on the way to succeed the ID.4 (and the ID.5 in markets where that's sold). And it looks like Volkswagen has taken some of the criticism to heart.
For starters, the ID. Tiguan has an upgraded infotainment and software stack. There are up to three screens now, including one directly in front of the passenger for apps and entertainment. The driver’s display and center screen are bigger and can be switched to a special “retro” mode that has stylized virtual gauge clusters from old Volkswagen models from the past. It’s the same system we’ve seen on the new ID. Polo.
Oh, and Volkswagen highlights that there are many more actual buttons now. There are new physical button pads on the steering wheel, as well as a row of buttons just below the main infotainment screen. A volume knob is back, right on the center console. That’s a big improvement over the annoying, touch-sensitive sliders dating back to the ID.4’s launch. The infamous push-for-rear window switches are gone, replaced with four traditional ones. 
The ID. Tiguan also gets handy EV-specific features the ID.4 never had. The crossover gains a frunk—albeit a tiny one with just 1.1 cubic feet of storage space. It gets one-pedal driving. And VW has added vehicle-to-load functionality, accessed via an outlet adapter that plugs into the charging port.
Stylistically, the ID. Tiguan comes off like a more mature version of the ID.4. The hood visually looks longer and more upright, while the side surfacing gives off a more expensive vibe. The interior looks to be a real upgrade, with Alcantara or suede surfaces on the R-line model.
On Friday, Volkswagen only released the European-spec ID. Tiguan deets. Powertrains are similar to what you'd find in the old ID.4; the ID. Tiguan is available in rear-wheel drive or all-wheel drive, with two different battery sizes.
The smaller 58 kWh battery produces 187 horsepower and is RWD only. The larger 77 kWh pack comes with either 282 horsepower in RWD form or 294 horsepower in AWD 4Motion trim. Maximum range is advertised at up to 600 kilometers (372 miles) for the 77 kWh model in RWD trim, based on the WLTP cycle. That's 26 km more than ID.4's rating in Europe, suggesting the U.S. model might get a range boost too.
Pricing starts at about 42,695 euros (about $49,000), which is roughly the same as what the current ID.4 costs in many European markets.
And yes, the ID. Tiguan is coming to the U.S. market too, a Volkswagen spokesperson said. The European version of the ID. Tiguan will launch in early 2027. Volkswagen told us that it will share U.S.-specific details sometime after that.
